name: Kadmiel
overview: Kadmiel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted primarily as the son of Hodaviah. His significance is highlighted by the fact that his descendants returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, marking his lineage's role in the restoration of the Jewish people. This connection situates Kadmiel within the post-exilic community rebuilding their covenantal identity.
namesAndTitles: The name Kadmiel means '[stand] before G-d [El],' reflecting a position of service or presence before God. This proper name, as recorded in Ezra 2:40, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication of dedication.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Kadmiel as the son of Hodaviah in Ezra 2:40. There is also an inferred relationship of Kadmiel being the father of Jeshua, as mentioned in Nehemiah 12:24. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Kadmiel's importance lies in his role as an ancestor whose descendants participated in the return to Judah following the Babylonian exile. This return was a pivotal moment in biblical history, restoring the worship and community life of Israel. By being part of the Levitical lineage, Kadmiel's family contributed to reestablishing the priestly and temple services central to Israel's faith.
